key_insight: Shared selective persistent memory lets agentic LLM systems retain only reusable work context—task specs, schemas, tool configs, and output constraints—while discarding noisy session traces, improving collaboration and completion.
engineering_relevance: This design reduces token waste and rework in deployed LLM workflows, enabling shared, role-controlled workspaces and zero-token data refresh for reusable, versioned artifacts.
method: Selectively persist four reusable context types instead of full chat history.
Share workspaces across users with role-based access control.
Decouple generated programs from runtime data to support zero-token refresh.
evidence_signal: Across three enterprise scenarios, the approach achieved 96% task completion versus 79% without memory and 71% with full-history persistence; zero-token refresh gave 14x faster recurring updates and 97x lower token cost, and 12/12 public-dataset trials succeeded.
watch_item: Selective memory must be carefully curated and governed, since incorrect retention or access control could preserve stale constraints or expose sensitive workspace context.
paper_title: Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems
